text: One freezing winter, Emperor Akbar made a bet. Any man who could stand all night in the icy palace lake would win a thousand gold coins.
A poor washerman took the challenge. He shivered and shook, all night long, and by morning, he was still standing!
How did you survive? asked Akbar. I kept my eyes on a lamp, burning far away in the palace, said the man.
Aha! said Akbar. So that lamp kept you warm. No reward for you!
The next day, Birbal didn't come to court. So Akbar went looking for him, and found him cooking khichdi.
But the pot was tied high up in a tree, and the tiny fire was far below, on the ground.
Birbal! laughed Akbar. That will never cook! Why not, Jahanpanah? said Birbal. If a lamp far away can warm a man in a lake, surely this fire can cook my khichdi.
Akbar laughed until he cried, and the washerman got every coin.
